Latin word

īnscrīptiō

īnscrīptiō, īnscrīptiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

an address (on a letter, for email); the writing on something, an inscription; title (what is written on a book); an inscription

In this lexicon

  • address

    the recommended word · modern · Traupman 268: īnscrīptiō cursuālis; Traupman 261, 309: īnscrīptiō ēlectronica, e-mail address; M-O s.v. address: inscriptio cursualis

  • sign

    also used · classical · Cic. Dom. 51: nōminis īnscrīptiō (Lewis & Short)

  • title

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 16.11.4; Traupman 395; M-O s.v. title (of book, article)

  • īnscrīptiō ēlectronica: email address

    modern

  • īnscrīptiō interrētiālis: URL

    modern

Examples

  • Unde est? — Tantundem. — Ubi habitat? — Nē id quidem.

    Where’s she from? — No idea either. — Where does she live? — I don’t even know that.Ter. Eun. 320c–321

    In the entry for address

  • tū fasciculum, quī est M’. Curiō īnscrīptus, velim cūrēs ad eum perferendum

    please see that the packet addressed to Manius Curius gets to himCic. Att. 8.5.2

    In the entry for address

  • numerus cursuālis (dīrēctōrius)

    a zip code, postcodeTraupman 410

    In the entry for address

  • quod dē īnscrīptiōne quaeris, nōn dubitō quīn καθῆκον officium sit, nisi quid tū aliud; sed īnscrīptiō plēnior dē officiīs.

    As for your question about the title: I have no doubt that καθῆκον is officium, unless you think otherwise; but the fuller title is De officiis.Cic. Att. 16.11.4
